newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends mostly firm, bear-spread hits Dec.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends mostly firm, bear-spread hits Dec.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended mostly firm on a mixture of export hopes and short covering before Thursday's USDA December crop report, but traders said bear-spreading pressured nearby Dec.

Wheat drew support Wednesday from a U.S. Wheat Associates analyst's projection that India may need to import one million tonnes of wheat in coming months. Wheat also was underpinned by ideas that Russia and Iraq could buy U.S. wheat.
KCBT wheat closed 1-3/4 cents per bushel higher to five cents lower, with December down 1-3/4 cents at $4.50-1/4. March lost 3-1/4 cents to close at $4.01-3/4.

December was under pressure as cash basis levels softened, triggering profit taking in the inverted Dec/March spread. Traders said commission houses were strong buyers in the March and May contracts ahead of the USDA report.
"This is mostly a market that's preparing for tomorrow's reports, and I think that's why you saw the funds in there squaring their positions," a trader said during the session.

E D & F Man International bear-spread 1.8 million May/March at 33 to 35 cents, traders said, while FIMAT was an outright buyer of two million March and CIS sold 2.2 million March. Prudential also bought one million March.
